People with diabetes need regular doses of insulin. Earlier, insulin was extracted from the pancreas of slaughtered cattle and pigs. Human insulin is made of two short polypeptide chains, chain A and chain B, linked by disulphide bridges. In the body it is first made as a pro-hormone that contains an extra stretch called the C peptide, which is removed during maturation. In 1983, an American company prepared two DNA sequences corresponding to the A and B chains of human insulin and introduced them into plasmids of E. coli. The two chains were produced separately, extracted and combined to form human insulin.
(a) State one problem caused by the use of insulin obtained from animal sources.
(b) What is the C peptide? Is it present in mature insulin?
(c) Why was it an advantage to produce chains A and B separately in E. coli?
OR
(c) What is gene therapy? Name the genetic disorder for which it was first used, and the enzyme that is deficient in this disorder.

A small herd of deer was introduced on an island that had plenty of grass and no predators. For the first few years the number of deer increased slowly, then it rose very rapidly. As the herd grew larger, grass became scarce, and the growth slowed down. Finally the population became almost steady at about 1000 deer, the largest number that the island could support. When ecologists plotted the number of deer against time, they obtained an S-shaped curve.
(a) What name is given to the maximum population size that a habitat can support?
(b) Write the equation that describes this type of population growth and name the type of growth.
(c) Why can a population not keep growing exponentially for a long time in nature?
OR
(c) At a time when the island had 200 deer, the intrinsic rate of natural increase was 0.1 per year. Using K = 1000, calculate the rate of growth of the population (dN/dt) at that time.
